decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Curative Title Risk as a Valuation Adjustment
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 687581b6137f8455ab24b6f398293e6a986bb16fb95120ebe0529b4e33d277cd; all 8 declared official sources passed live access review.
Recording, conveyance, succession, payment-suspense, agency-jurisdiction, property-tax income-analysis, and archival-record claims remain bounded to their official Texas sources.
The article uses no fabricated documents, owner facts, legal conclusions, cure deadlines, dollar amounts, percentages, title standards, testimonials, or owner-specific value conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Natural Resources Code Chapter 91, including Section 91.402 (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 addresses time for payment and circumstances involving title disputes, reasonable doubt as to clear title, and unsatisfied curative requirements.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The statute supports payment and suspense context; it does not determine private ownership, prescribe a sale-price adjustment, or supply an owner-specific title conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Property Code Chapter 13, Effects of Recording (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Sections 13.001 and 13.002 address unrecorded instruments and the notice and inspection effects of instruments properly recorded in the proper county.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the chapter for recording context and does not treat an index search or recorded instrument alone as a complete owner-specific title conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Property Code Chapter 5, Conveyances (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 5 contains rules governing conveyances of real property and the instruments and disclosures used in that setting.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The source supports reviewing actual conveyance language and related instruments; the article does not decide what a particular deed conveyed or reserved.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Estates Code Chapter 101, Estate Assets in General (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Estates Code Section 101.001 states that estate property generally vests immediately at death in devisees or heirs, subject to Section 101.051 and administration-related provisions.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves those statutory qualifications and does not claim that a death, missing filing, or vesting rule proves a transaction-ready ownership chain.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas authority and jurisdiction (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission states that oil and gas leases and agreements, pipeline easements, and royalty payments are outside its jurisdiction.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The source supports the jurisdiction boundary; regulatory records are not presented as private ownership or title determinations.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas royalties FAQ (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission royalty FAQ explains that lease and royalty matters are private matters outside Commission authority and summarizes payment and title-suspense provisions.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page for public payment context and does not ask the Commission source to resolve a private title dispute or transaction value.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller Manual for Discounting Oil and Gas Income (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller manual documents an income-discounting framework for Texas oil and gas property-tax appraisal, including amount, timing, discounting, and risk inputs.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves the property-tax context and does not present the manual as a private-sale formula, cure-cost schedule, or owner-specific valuation.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office search collections (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas General Land Office provides searchable historical land-grant, map, surname-index, and archival collections for Texas land research.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article presents those collections as supplemental historical and survey evidence, not a replacement for county records, controlling private instruments, or professional title review.
